title: You May Not Take It Straight Back
intro: There is one more rule and I put it off because it is the strange one.

Sometimes a capture leaves a position where the other player could immediately capture back, and then you could capture back, and so on until one of you died of old age. So there is a rule against it, and it is called ko.

steps.instruction: That single white stone has one liberty. Take it.
steps.explanation: One stone captured. Now look at the stone you just played -- it has one liberty of its own, and White would very much like to take it back the same way. This shape is a ko.

steps.instruction: White has just taken your stone. Take it straight back.
steps.hint: Try it. The game will refuse you.
steps.explanation: Refused. You may not recreate the position that was on the board a moment ago. You have to play somewhere else first -- and if that somewhere else is a threat White must answer, you get to come back and take the ko after all. That is a ko fight, and it is the only part of Go that feels like an argument.

outro: Play elsewhere, then take it back. That is the whole rule.
Kesh loves ko. I find it stressful and I lose them, so do not take my word for how to win one -- only for what is and is not allowed.
